text:
Jordan: heads-up — I ran a 2h perf sweep on the new adaptive bucketizer and hit a weird regression for short, high-decode-rate prompts. p95 latency jumped ~30% after the kernel handoff kicked in :confused:

Maria: can you paste the profile? did kernel selection fallback to the generic kernel or a quantized path?

Jordan: putting the TL;DR first — when decode-rate > 350 tokens/s and prompt_len < 64, the classifier sometimes routes to kernel_v2 which has worse L1 cache behavior for tiny KV hits. full trace below.

Sam: ack. sounds like a signal misalignment between the decode-rate bucket and the token_budget target. our batch formation expects larger microbatches there. can you share the queue snapshot?

Jordan: sure — snippet from the node logs (condensed):
```
[2035127891] queue: pending=18, avg_prompt_len=42, avg_decode_rate=410
[2035127891] bucketizer: chosen_bucket=short_fast, token_budget_target=256
[2035127891] kernel_handoff: prefer=kernel_v2, fallback=kernel_v1
[2035127892] kv: prefetch=on, hit_rate=0.42, thrash_count=12
[2035127893] batcher: formed_microbatch=6, latency_ms=120
[2035127893] runtime: p95_latency_ms=210 (baseline=160)
```

Anya: kv hit rate 0.42 for those short prompts is suspicious — prefetch might be warming irrelevant keys. Could be evicting hot keys for subsequent longer requests.

Maria: agree. If kernel_v2 has heuristics that assume hotter KV access, prefetch + small token_budget could cause poor locality. Two immediate ideas: 1) raise token_budget_target for short_fast bucket to 512, 2) disable aggressive prefetch for <64 tokens.

Sam: +1 for increasing token_budget_target, but we should simulate impact on batch formation. bigger token_budget => larger microbatches => increased latency tail for interactive flows if we overshoot. we need a narrow experiment.

Jordan: Proposed experiment A/B: on 10% of pods, change short_fast token_budget_target 256->512; on another 10%, keep token_budget but force kernel_v1 for short_fast. Collect: p50/p95 latency, tokens/s, KV hit rate, GPU util, batch sizes distribution. Run for 3 hours.

Maria: add a probe to record kernel selection reasons (metrics: score_diff, fallback_trigger). put a tag so we can join traces: tag=bucketizer-adaptive-v2test

Anya: I'll add a small change to the prefetcher to only prefetch if predicted_kv_score > 0.7 for short prompts. low risk toggle.

dev-bot: deploy queued: rollout bucketizer-adaptive-v2test -> 20% canaries across us-west/us-east. CI checks passed. :rocket:

Sam: question on classifier thresholds — what features are we using? currently it's [prompt_len, decode_rate, kv_hit_estimate, model_variant]. maybe add last_batch_kv_hit_avg to smooth spikey hit rates?

Jordan: yes that might stabilize decisions. right now the classifier uses instantaneous decode_rate which fluctuates. smoothing with an EWMA (alpha=0.2) for kv_hit_estimate + last_batch_kv_hit_avg should reduce oscillation.

Maria: also consider a guard: if batcher formed_microbatch < 4 and prompt_len < 64, prefer kernel_v1 regardless of decode_rate. cheap rule but avoids thrash while we iterate.

Anya: noted. I'll implement the kernel override + prefetch toggle. Sam, can you own the analytics dashboard query to compare A/B? need p95 by cohort, kv_hit_rate, and kernel_fallback_rate.

Sam: on it. I'll add a cohort filter for tag=bucketizer-adaptive-v2test and create dashboard panels. ETA 2h.

Jordan: thanks. action items: Maria — add selection-reason metric; Anya — prefetch toggle + kernel override; Sam — dashboard; I'll run the rollout and collect traces. regroup after 3h with numbers. :thumbsup:

Maria: one more note — if we see perf improve but tokens/sec drops, we should run a cost analysis before changing defaults. Redwood Optimize will want the delta.

Jordan: good call. I'll export token-cost delta as part of the report.

Anya: leaving a quick test command here for the canary nodes: `curl -H \"x-bucketizer:short_fast\" http://node-canary.local/probe?payload=short_high_rate` — returns perf counters in header for quick spot checks.

Jordan: perfect. will run. thanks everyone. :eyes:
